Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 4-day history of viral prodrome progressing from sore throat → rhinorrhoea/nasal congestion → dry cough, with transient fever, myalgias, headache, night sweats, and mild exertional dyspnoea.  
• No red-flag symptoms (no persistent high fever, no chest pain, no rest dyspnoea).  
• Most consistent with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory tract infection. Influenza or mild COVID-19 also possible; patient advised to monitor symptoms and seek review if deterioration.  
• No contradiction between transcript and DDx identified.

Management Plan
- Advise rest, increased oral fluids, continue paracetamol and ibuprofen PRN  
- Consider 1–2 days off work  
- Safety-net advice: return or call sooner for high fever, worsening cough or breathlessness, chest pain, or no improvement by next week  
- No medications, tests, or referrals initiated at this time

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – High likelihood: symptom sequence, mild course, improving.  
2. Influenza – Moderate likelihood: initial fever, myalgias, headache; less likely as fever resolved quickly.  
3. COVID-19 (mild) – Moderate likelihood: overlapping symptoms including night sweats and exertional dyspnoea; lacks loss of taste/smell.
